skill.name: baoyu-comic
skill.description: Creates educational comics from source material. It analyzes content, builds storyboards and character sheets, writes image prompts, and can merge finished pages into a PDF.
skill.summary: Turn articles, lessons, and biographies into structured comic projects with storyboards, character references, prompts, and PDF output.
skill.author: JimLiu

security_audit.summary: The scanner mostly matched benign Markdown backticks, TypeScript template literals, and visual layout terms. I found one contextual concern: the documented PDF step uses `npx -y bun`, which can fetch and run an unpinned external tool. No prompt-injection text, network exfiltration, or hidden reconnaissance intent was found.

remediation.issue: Unpinned external tool invocation in the PDF workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Replace `npx -y bun` with a pinned, documented runtime requirement or a local package script using locked dependencies.

remediation.issue: Filesystem changes need clear user consent.
remediation.suggestion: Before renaming, deleting, or overwriting project files, require explicit user confirmation and show the target paths.

remediation.issue: The PDF script accepts user-provided input and output paths.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve paths under the comic project directory unless the user explicitly confirms an external output path.

static_findings.snippet: Avoid AI-style "Title: Subtitle" format. Use narrative descriptions:
| `--style` | classic (default), dramatic, warm, tech, sepia, vibrant, ohmsha, realistic, or custom
| `--layout` | standard (default), cinematic, dense, splash, mixed, webtoon |
**Important**: All scripts are located in the `scripts/` subdirectory of this skill.
1. Determine this SKILL.md file's directory path as `SKILL_DIR`
3. Replace all `${SKILL_DIR}` in this document with the actual path
- If target directory exists, rename existing to `<dirname>-backup-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`
- If user pastes content: save to `source.md` in target directory
- `characters.md` - visual specs matching the recommended style (in user's preferred language)
4. If style differs from variant's recommended: regenerate `characters/characters.png`
1. Save prompt to `prompts/NN-{cover|page}-[slug].md` (in user's preferred language)
- If skill supports reference image: pass `characters/characters.png`
- If skill does NOT support reference image: include `characters/characters.md` content in prompt
Creates `{topic-slug}.pdf` with all pages as full-page images.
2. Create new prompt with appropriate slug (e.g., `04-page-bletchley-park.md`)
- Custom characters only if explicitly requested: `--characters "Student:小明,Mentor:教授"`
Detailed templates and guidelines in `references/` directory:
- `analysis-framework.md` - Deep content analysis for comic adaptation

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned External Tool Execution
semantic_findings.description: The PDF step tells the agent to run `npx -y bun`, which can download and execute an unpinned external tool without confirmation. This creates a supply chain risk during normal skill use.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command is explicitly documented in the normal PDF workflow and uses npx with automatic confirmation. It appears intended, not malicious, so medium severity is appropriate.

content.user_title: Create Knowledge Comics From Source Material
content.value_statement: Long source material is hard to turn into clear visual lessons. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through analysis, storyboarding, image prompts, and PDF assembly.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes source material for audience, themes, characters, and page count.
Creates three storyboard variants with different narrative approaches.
Builds character reference sheets and prompt files for generated pages.
Supports classic, dramatic, warm, tech, sepia, vibrant, Ohmsha, and realistic styles.
Supports standard, cinematic, dense, splash, mixed, and webtoon layouts.
Merges completed page images into a PDF with the included script.
limitations: It depends on an available image generation tool for artwork.
It does not verify facts beyond the provided source unless asked.
Large projects may require several manual review cycles.
The PDF merge step runs a local script and needs compatible runtime support.

use_cases.title: Convert lessons into comic teaching aids
use_cases.description: Create storyboards and visual prompts for tutorials, technical concepts, or classroom explainers.

use_cases.title: Adapt biographies into narrative comics
use_cases.description: Turn long articles into page plans, character sheets, and consistent visual direction.

use_cases.title: Explain complex research visually
use_cases.description: Prepare dense concepts as approachable panels with style and layout guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Create a beginner comic
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a short educational comic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use baoyu-comic on this source. Create a short educational comic in English with the recommended style and layout.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a visual direction
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with user confirmation before images.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this source, propose three storyboard variants, and ask me to choose style, layout, language, and aspect ratio.

prompt_templates.title: Build a technical webtoon
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a dense technical topic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a webtoon-style knowledge comic about this technical topic. Use dense explanations, visual metaphors, and consistent character references.

prompt_templates.title: Revise an existing comic project
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for page insertion and PDF rebuild.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the existing comic folder, add one page after page three, renumber files, update prompts, and rebuild the PDF.

output_examples.input: A teacher provides a chapter about neural networks.
output_examples.output: The skill returns an analysis, three storyboard choices, character plans, and page prompts for an educational comic.

output_examples.input: A writer asks for a biography comic about Alan Turing.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes chronological, thematic, and character-focused versions with matching styles and page counts.

output_examples.input: A user has finished page images and wants a PDF.
output_examples.output: The skill runs the merge workflow and reports the PDF name, page count, and project location.

best_practices: Review the analysis and storyboard before generating images.
Keep one aspect ratio for all pages in the same comic.
Use character references or written character specs for visual consistency.
anti_patterns: Skipping user confirmation for storyboard, style, language, or aspect ratio.
Generating pages before the source analysis and storyboard are complete.
Mixing unrelated visual styles across pages without a reason.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates structured comic projects with analysis, storyboards, character references, prompts, images, and optional PDF output.

faq.question: Does it generate images itself?
faq.answer: It prepares prompts and uses available image generation skills or tools to create page images.

faq.question: Can I choose the style?
faq.answer: Yes. You can choose built-in styles or give a custom style description.

faq.question: Can it work from pasted text?
faq.answer: Yes. It can save pasted content as source material in the project folder.

faq.question: Can it edit existing pages?
faq.answer: Yes. It can regenerate, insert, delete, and renumber pages when asked.

faq.question: Does it create a PDF?
faq.answer: Yes. After images exist, it can merge them into a full-page PDF.
